items.stem: Why is a complete AI use-case inventory foundational to governance?

options.text: You cannot govern or risk-assess systems you do not know exist
options.rationale: Correct: visibility of all use cases, including shadow AI, enables control.
Inventory is about oversight, not accuracy.

options.text: It replaces the need for any policy

items.stem: Which TWO practices make governance proportionate rather than bureaucratic? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Tier use cases by risk and apply controls accordingly
options.rationale: Correct: higher-risk cases get more scrutiny.

options.text: Place review gates at key lifecycle stages
options.rationale: Correct: gates focus oversight where decisions are made.

options.text: Require identical heavy review for every trivial use

items.explanation: Correct: higher-risk cases get more scrutiny.

items.stem: A governance dashboard reports 'number of committee meetings held'. Why is that a weak metric?

options.text: It measures activity, not whether AI risk is actually reduced
options.rationale: Correct: outcome metrics matter more than activity counts.
Meetings can be useful; the metric is just weak.

options.text: It is too hard to count
options.rationale: It is easy to count but not meaningful.
